# Problem statement

Suppose we have a data $X_1,\dots,X_n \sim D$ where $D$ is our data distribution. Suppose further that $X_i = [x_1 \quad \dots \quad x_m \quad y_i]^\top$ where $y_i$ is our label ($y_i\in \{0,1\}$ for simplicity). Then, with this finite observations $X_1,\dots,X_n$, we want to reconstruct $D$ with parameterized distribution $\tilde{D}(\theta)$ where $\theta \in \Theta_{1:n} = \Theta(X_1,\dots, X_n)$ that at least
$$ \mathbb{E}_{1:n}\left[\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_\mathcal{H}(D,\tilde{D}(\theta))\right] < \varepsilon $$

where $\mathbb{E}_{1:n}$ is expectation operator under finite sample. That said, $D$ is unknown. We could first invoke the triangle inequality of the metric $d_{\mathcal{H}}$ so that we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{1:n}\left[\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_\mathcal{H}(D, \tilde{D}(\theta))\right] \leq \mathbb{E}_{1:n}\left[d_\mathcal{H}(D,\tilde{0}) + \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_{\mathcal{H}}(\tilde{D}(\theta), \tilde{0})\right] $$

where $\tilde{0}\in\mathcal{H}$ which is some anchor point on the space $\mathcal{H}$. Same with other direction, that is

$$
\mathbb{E}_{1:n}\left[\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_\mathcal{H}(D, \tilde{D}(\theta))\right] \geq \mathbb{E}_{1:n}\left[d_\mathcal{H}(D,\tilde{0}) - \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_{\mathcal{H}}(\tilde{D}(\theta), \tilde{0})\right] 
$$

That implies
$$
\mathbb{E}_{1:N}\left[d_{\mathcal{H}}(D,\tilde{0}) - \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_{\mathcal{H}}(\tilde{D}(\theta), \tilde{0})\right] \leq \mathbb{E}_{1:n}\left[\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_\mathcal{H}(D,\tilde{D}(\theta))\right] \leq \mathbb{E}_{1:N}\left[d_{\mathcal{H}}(D,\tilde{0}) + \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_{\mathcal{H}}(\tilde{D}(\theta), \tilde{0})\right] 
$$

This is one of the interesting condition to think about
$$
\mathbb{E}_{1:N}\left[d_{\mathcal{H}}(D,\tilde{0})\right] > \mathbb{E}_{1:N}\left[\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{1:n}} d_{\mathcal{H}}(\tilde{D}(\theta), \tilde{0})\right]
$$
because if that is true for all $\tilde{0}\in \mathcal{H}$ then you can't reconstruct the distribution with the model exactly under metric $d_\mathcal{H}$. Now, suppose further that if we have a sequence of the model or observation, can we talk about the asymptotic behavior or show something (like $\limsup$ or $\liminf$ style of argument) to say that specific family of the model cannot, asymptotically, representing the "real" distribution under the metric $d_\mathcal{H}$?
